note: Hand-written headers that SHADOW the generated tree. An override is placed earlier on the include path than the generated include directory, so the generated file stays untouched and the override is the whole of the modification: the set of files under overrides/include is the diff, and no computation is needed to find it. Reserved for what the declared mechanisms cannot reach -- source-patches/ rewrites the pinned TypeScript, repairs/ adds text with no behavior to emitted output, and either is preferable because neither carries a copy. An override does carry a copy, so each entry records `derivedFrom`, the sha256 of the generated file it was produced from. When a pin move changes that file the digest stops matching and `npm run overrides:check` says so, which is the signal to re-derive the override or drop it. Each entry also carries a `status`: `complete` means the override compiles, `incomplete` means it is partway and says what remains, so nobody mistakes a half-finished override for a finished one.

A repair cannot change a type representation or supply identity semantics; both are behavioral emitter/runtime decisions rather than text-only insertions.
overrides.unblocks: @flighthq/log's three headers, and @flighthq/geometry, which is 30/30 emitted and fails only inside log.hpp. log is the second-largest cascade root in the SDK at nineteen packages. The identity-bearing carrier also closes log's two remaining semantic divergences: duplicate registration and removal through a copied callback.
overrides.expires: when the emitter lowers Readonly<LogEntry> consistently in aliases and lambda parameters and represents JavaScript function values with an identity-bearing callable such as flight::Function.

overrides.reason: The emitter refused connectSignalDebounced and connectSignalThrottled (cpp-dependent-parameter-pack-nonterminal-use: their `any[]` lastArgs buffer names the slot's callable parameter pack as storage), and in the emitted connectSignalAtFrameRate it wrote `elapsed %= period` as a C++ remainder on double, so throttle.hpp and both aggregators fail to compile. That handler is also a bare lambda erased into std::function, whose identity callable_identity_equal cannot recover, so its cleanup's disconnect throws.
overrides.change: Supplies both connectors with the slot's own parameter tuple, std::optional<std::tuple<Args...>>, as the argument buffer, replayed by std::apply; reads leading/trailing through the same optional row access the emitter uses for connectSignal options; uses flight::host::set_timeout/clear_timeout and flight::Date::now as the bindings do. In connectSignalAtFrameRate, replaces `%=` with std::fmod. Every handler is a flight::Function so cleanup disconnects the exact callable it connected.
overrides.equivalence: The buffer stores exactly the arguments the slot received, without erasure, and replays them in order. Option defaults are the source's (debounce leading false, trailing true; throttle both true). The timer, clock and branch structure follow the source line for line, including resetting leadingFired and the timer before the trailing call, clearing lastArgs after it, -Infinity as the initial lastFiredAt, and the `remaining <= 0 || remaining > intervalMs` test. std::fmod has JavaScript `%` semantics on finite numbers (truncation toward zero, dividend sign). Spreading a null buffer throws TypeError, as `slot(...lastArgs!)` does when lastArgs is null. Cleanup disconnects the same handler and clears any pending timer.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A source rewrite that keeps the public generic signature cannot remove the variadic buffer: parameterizing the connector over one payload type, as the refusal suggests, changes the exported API. A repair may only add declarations without behavior. The `%=` and handler-identity defects are in the same file the override must copy anyway, so a separate patch would be a second debt instrument for one header.
overrides.unblocks: flight/signals/throttle.hpp, contract.hpp and _internal_index.hpp compile; together with connection.hpp this takes @flighthq/signals headers from 7/10.
overrides.remaining: None in throttle.ts at this pin.
overrides.expires: when the emitter stores a callable parameter pack as a typed tuple (or erases it faithfully), lowers compound `%=` on captured numeric bindings to fmod, and gives locally declared handlers callable identity.
